text:
Alex K.: heads-up — we're designing envelope flow for multi-tenant private deployments. question: recommended KEK separation strategy when customers bring their own KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure)?
Maria C.: short answer: keep KEK pointers per-tenant + per-region, use KMS only for KEK unwrap/wrap ops, never for per-request DEK unwrap where we can avoid it.
Sam P.: can you sketch the call frequency targets? e.g., our 99th percentile token path shouldn't hit KMS every request.
Alex K.: goal: KMS calls only on cold DEK fetch or rotation. cache DEKs in a local encrypted keystore with TTL + jitter. default TTL 1h for hot DEKs, 24h for less active tenants. add splay to avoid thundering herd.
Jen O.: +1. also add a per-tenant hotkey count: if a tenant exceeds X unwraps/min, escalate to rate-limited mode and sample unwraps (and route to dedicated KEK-backed pool).
EncryptorBot: reminder: GCP KMS has lower per-key QPS than AWS KMS; Azure Key Vault concurrent limits differ — factor these into backoff configs.
Sam P.: RBAC question: do we give service account decrypt rights on customer KEKs? or have a proxy that impersonates customers?
Maria C.: prefer proxy/impersonation where possible. pattern: Redwood KMS-proxy role has 'wrap/unwrap' on a tenant-owned key resource but we use short-lived impersonation tokens minted per-tenant. Audit logs still attribute to tenant key resource. Keeps cross-tenant elevation risk low.
Alex K.: for BYOK (customer-managed keys) we do explicit opt-in flow: customer grants our proxy principal minimal decrypt privileges and we store grant metadata in our audit DB. no blanket org-wide perms.
Jen O.: about audit logging: we need high-fidelity unwrap events (who, which tenant, request id, reason code). suggestion: sink KMS audit + local keystore decisions to separate immutable store (retention 1y by default), sample payloads for privacy.
Sam P.: what about encryption-at-rest for cached DEKs? storing plaintext DEKs in memory is fine, but on-disk cache must be wrapped by a platform master key (HSM-backed) or local envelope.
Maria C.: exactly — store cached DEKs encrypted with a platform KEK stored in HSM/KMS (not customer KEK). rotate platform KEK quarterly and rewrap during maintenance windows.
Alex K.: incident plan if KMS unavailable: 1) if tenant is on dedicated SLA allow local keystore fallback (DEK cache) for short window (configurable), 2) otherwise fail closed — deny unwrap ops. On-call should have runbook to enable emergency fallback per-account with approval audit.
Oncall SRE: propose an automated safe-guard: require two-person approval to temporarily enable per-tenant fallback, write an audit entry and alert #incidents.
EncryptorBot: ops note: implement token-bucket smoothing for KMS calls, and an exponential backoff with jitter for unwrap retries. emit metrics: kms_unwrap_rate, kube_keystore_hits, cache_miss_latency.
Jen O.: config example for keystore policy: 
```yaml
keystore:
  cache_ttl_seconds: 3600 # default
  cold_ttl_seconds: 86400
  splay_seconds: 300
  max_unwraps_per_min: 500 # per-tenant hotkey threshold
  backoff:
    base_ms: 100
    max_ms: 20000
```
Alex K.: ops + security action items: 1) update RBAC doc to include proxy impersonation flow + sample IAM policies (AWS/GCP/Azure), 2) add unwrap audit schema to logging playbook, 3) implement retry/backoff + token-bucket, 4) add runbook steps for emergency fallback with two-person approval.
Maria C.: I'll draft the RBAC snippets for AWS KMS (kms:Decrypt on key resource), GCP IAM condition examples, and Azure Key Vault RBAC role assignment templates.
Sam P.: I'll prototype the keystore cache with deterministic splay and token bucket, then run perf tests against simulated KMS QPS limits.
Alex K.: thanks — ping me when drafts are ready. :thumbsup:
